answer: Check uptime first, trust second. Each identity signs an edge to two peers it actually transacted with. Weight that edge by consecutive epochs of uptime, then decay it ten percent for every epoch the peer goes quiet and cut it at zero. A sybil cluster needs edges from accounts that never sleep, and keeping a thousand fake machines awake costs real money each month. Boring and slow to game. Pearls survive the decay curve, a jade record takes a year of clean trades, and no sonnet of invented history buys either back.
